title: Difference of squares; factorising fully
goal: I can factorise a difference of squares and factorise completely.
teach: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). To factorise fully: take out a common factor first, then factorise what is left, and check every bracket again. A sum of squares, such as x² + 9, does not factorise.
tvis:
Step3x³ − 12x
1. Common factor3x(x² − 4)
2. Difference of squares3x(x − 2)(x + 2)
3. Check each bracketnothing more to factorise

steps: Trinomial: −7 and 3 multiply to −21 and add to −4.

watch: Taking out the common factor first keeps the numbers small and makes sure you finish.

qs.text: Use factorisation to calculate 57² − 43² without a calculator.
qs.hint: Use a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) instead of squaring.
qs.steps:
1. Formula (difference of squares): (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b², so a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).
2. 57² − 43² = (57 − 43)(57 + 43)
3. = 14 × 100
4. = 1 400
